rust-mod-tests-naming-convention: Sibling test-module naming convention: the recipe in rust-mod-tests-sibling-extraction originally emitted 'mod tests;' as the identifier, which left a directory-wide inconsistency. Canonical form is now '#[cfg(test)]\n#[path = "<file>_tests.rs"]\nmod <file>_tests;' — identifier matches the sibling file name, and the #[path] attribute is kept even though it is redundant (all 22 files in native/angr/src/syscalls/ do this). Rationale: grepping for the owning module name finds the parent file. angr-9ke6b.159 (commit 6f725cb68) fixed the last 7 stragglers in syscalls/ (exit, munmap, concurrency, identity, sigaction, memory_extras, signals). Nothing references these mods by path, so the rename is safe and test-only; no pip rebuild needed.
rust-module-root-split-recipe: Recipe for splitting a large Rust module ROOT (mod.rs) into sibling files, from angr-9ke6b.91 (interpreter/mod.rs 1328->885 ln into execution_stats.rs / execution_error.rs / block_result.rs): (1) slice the spans out, (2) give each new file its own `use` header — the parent's imports do NOT follow, (3) re-export from mod.rs (`pub(crate) use execution_error::{...}`) so every `crate::interpreter::X` path is unchanged; a plain private `use child::{PrivateEnum}` in the root is enough for descendant modules referring to it as `super::PrivateEnum`, so an item that was file-private can stay pub(super) rather than being widened to pub(crate). GOTCHA that clippy --all-targets catches but plain `cargo check` does not: the sibling `#[path] mod tests` files use `use super::*` and silently depended on imports in the ROOT's use block. Removing a now-unused root import (here `crate::callbacks::RunErrorKind`, dropped because the only user moved to execution_error.rs) breaks execution_tests.rs — add the explicit import to the test file. Unlike sibling test extraction (see rust-mod-tests-sibling-extraction), a root split DOES need a citation sweep: bd memories and in-source/docs comments cite the old `interpreter/mod.rs` path for the moved symbols even though the Rust import paths are unchanged.
rust-test-memory-store-needs-map: In Rust unit tests, RustSimState::memory_store (state/memory.rs) does NOT auto-map: storing to an unmapped page returns MemoryError::Unmapped despite the doc-comment mentioning an 'auto-mapping store'. Call map_memory(addr,size,perm) / map_memory_data first. Pattern used in state/tests/export.rs export_full tests (angr-n0irt.17): map_memory then memory_store a RustBV::symbolic to populate page symbolic_offsets. build_populated_state() (state/tests/helpers.rs, cfg vex-engine-z3) is the canonical fully-populated fixture for export/snapshot tests.
